correctness.rationale: For even k=2m, the exact period gcd G=gcd(F_{k+1}-1,F_{k+2}-1)=U_m follows from standard addition identities; the cubic Cassini congruence and local valuations give D=gcd(F_{k+1}^3−1,F_{k+2}^3−1)=3^{[4|m]}G. The all-shift cube differences share gcd D; the telescoping initial sum S_0 gives gcd(D,S_0)=D/2 exactly when 3|m, otherwise D. This gives the stated infinite-window formula, including C_3(6)=2, C_3(8)=9. Independently computed exact 14-window gcds for 120 even lengths; these only corroborate the proof. Read two earlier full independent mathematical proofs, one for every even Fibonacci AND Lucas cubic window and the other for every positive Fibonacci cubic window.

value.rationale: The higher-power Fibonacci window GCD is motivated by an explicit prior open question, and the formula is mathematically meaningful, but both Nov 2 primary results already solve this very even-window formula (one also Lucas, one all k). This later duplicate does not supply a novel invariant, family extension, bound or mathematical insight qualifying independently as research value.

final_claim: For every even positive window length 2m, the gcd over all starts n≥0 of sums of 2m successive cubes of standard Fibonacci numbers equals 3^{[4|m]} U_m / 2^{[3|m]}, with U_m=F_m for even m and L_m for odd m.
limitations: Only standard Fibonacci cubes at even window lengths; no Lucas or odd length novelty, as both are already covered by earlier papers. Finite shift-window GCDs are not exhaustive.
